_doc: Which shared gates have PROVEN they can fail, and how.
READ BY checks/check_probes_pass.py, through checks/_calibration.py. Every entry is verified
against the estate before this file is believed: the key must name a gate that exists, a cited
prover must resolve and be COMMITTED, and a prover inside this repo must have had its claimed
self-proof run green by the same sweep. An entry naming no gate, no file, no commit or no
running proof is a FINDING (SUPERSOTA R7: a registry nothing reads is a rumour).
These gates run in four repos, so their proof belongs HERE rather than inside any one
consumer -- two of them were canaried from inside ZeroThunder, which meant the other three
inherited the gate without the evidence.
proven_by: the canary runs each check against a git repo containing a real violation and
asserts it goes RED, then against a clean tree and asserts GREEN. Red-on-violation is the
load-bearing half: a gate that scans nothing exits 0 and is indistinguishable from a gate
that scanned everything, and two fixtures in this very table were silently out of scope
Keys name the gate WITHOUT its check_ prefix, and a prose claim that names no prover file
(an in-selftest: entry) is left to the sweep rather than resolved here. Regenerate the canary
citations with the canary, never by hand -- a registry a human types is a registry that

proven_by.version_provenance: tests/test_check_version_provenance.py (the native `goh version-provenance`, run by this repo's push gate): red on a version with no commit and no date; a version declared in src/lib.rs is REACHED rather than read as not-applicable; an opaque clause field whose build script never asks about the working tree is red; a baseline entry naming a file the checker never reads is a FINDING; green on a truthful version
proven_by.lock_version: tests/test_check_lock_version.py (the native `goh lock-version`, run by this repo's push gate): app_updates' real 2026-10-01 shape -- manifest 1.36.0, Cargo.lock 1.35.0, both members INHERITING -- is red; regenerating the lockfile is green; a release number bumped in one place only is red; per-crate versions are a layout and produce no finding; a member list spread over lines is read whole and an exclude below it is not mistaken for a member
proven_by.md_links: tests/test_check_md_links.py (the native `goh md-links`, run by this repo's push gate): the audit's hand-mis-derived anchor (#48-what-90-can-actually-do-measured) is red and the right one is green; a missing file is red; a link in an inline code span, a fenced block or an indented block is an example and produces nothing
proven_by.no_empty_assert: tests/test_check_no_empty_assert.py (the native `goh empty-assert`, run by this repo's push gate; the measured clippy 1.99.0 table of 2026-10-02 is a Rust test beside the port): the six shapes clippy reports AND the two it is silent on, `assert!(x.is_empty(), "msg")` and `assert!(!x.is_empty(), "msg")`, which is why the gate exists at all; the forms clippy tells you to write (`assert_eq!(x.len(), 0)`, `assert_ne!`) stay green; a multi-line chain is reported at its `assert!` line; a `)` inside a message does not end the scan
proven_by.no_unreaped_spawn: tests/test_unreaped_spawn_native_parity.py (the native `goh unreaped-spawn`, run by this repo's push gate): the MEASURED table, 55 shapes in tests/unreaped_spawn_table*.py, each disposition measured against rustc 1.99.0 by a pid-liveness probe on 2026-10-03 (spawn+drop = LIVE orphan; kill without wait = ZOMBIE; a guard reaps through a panic; output()/status() BLOCK instead of leaking), every row's whole verdict list equal to the frozen reference's. The incident itself is a case, QUOTED from media_server at 052772a: red on the real pre-fix file naming the first panicking line and the reap below it, GREEN on the same file after its fix
proven_by.tag_version: tests/test_check_tag_version.py (the native `goh tag-version`, run by this repo's push gate): a pushed v<semver> tag whose commit declares another version is red; red on media_server's real 2026-10-01 shape (tag v1.79.3, commit declaring 1.79.1), green on a matching pair, and a tag with no version source is a finding
proven_by.claim_derivation: tests/test_check_claim_derivation.py (the native `goh claim-derivation`, run by this repo's push gate): every claim type red-before and green-after -- lines, tests, declared-by-name, files-by-extension, and the backtick spelling -- plus the negative controls that must stay quiet (a bare number beside a path, a version, a heading anchor, prose ABOUT a claim, a fenced example, an indented example). The estate's own defect is a case: a label carrying a second space is COUNTED, where the re.findall that read 64 against 70 matches 1 of 4 against the same roster. Every printed re-derivation command is EXECUTED against its fixture and compared with the number the gate returned. Ten unresolvable shapes are findings naming why, not skips; the allowlist ratchet is proven in both directions
proven_by.no_credential_urls: tests/test_credential_urls_native_parity.py (the native `goh credential-urls`, run by this repo's push gate): the MEASURED table is 26 shapes -- 22 remote-URL forms read back through git's own config reader and CPython urlsplit, plus 4 about the KEY rather than the URL -- each row's verdict equal to the frozen reference's. Green on `ssh://git@github.com/...`, on `git@github.com:o/r.git`, on `file://`, a local path, `git://`, an IPv6 literal and `https://someuser@github.com/...`; RED on `https://user:gho_<36>@...`, on the bare `https://gho_<36>@...` shape, and on an `ssh://` remote carrying a token. The report carries a sha256 fingerprint and never the value, pinned by a planted credential (tests/test_check_no_credential_urls.py)
